brief.title: Midterm brief: Sunday, October 11
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Sunday, October 11

## Bottom line

Twenty-three days out, forecasters and markets agree on the shape of the race but not the outcome. The House leans Democratic: nine of ten forecasters on the Wikipedia ratings table project more Democratic than Republican seats before tossups, and Polymarket prices a Democratic House at 90.5% ([ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings), [market](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026)). The Senate is the contest: consensus ratings put Democrats at 46 seats solid or likely and Republicans at 45, with nine Lean-to-Tossup races deciding a 51-seat majority ([Senate ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Polymarket prices Democratic Senate control at 63.5% and a split Congress, Republican Senate with Democratic House, at 29.5% ([Senate](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026), [balance of power](https://polymarket.com/event/balance-of-power-2026-midterms)).

## What moved

Nothing crossed a movement threshold. This is a same-day rerun against this morning's baseline, so day-over-day tracking starts tomorrow.

## Races to watch today

- **Maine Senate (Tossup).** Troy Jackson leads Susan Collins 50 to 45 among likely voters in a Washington Post/George Mason poll, Sept. 30 to Oct. 5 (n=800); the 21-day average is D+2.1 across nine polls ([WaPo](https://www.washingtonpost.com/tablet/2026/10/09/sept-30-oct-5-2026-washington-post-schar-school-poll-maine-voters)). The New York Times reports Collins often defies Trump but rarely stops him ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/11/us/politics/in-the-senate-collins-often-defies-trump-but-rarely-stops-him.html)).
- **Ohio Senate special (Tossup).** CNN/SSRS has Sherrod Brown 49, Jon Husted 43 among likely voters through Oct. 5 (n=760); a Republican-sponsored co/efficient poll through Oct. 6 has Husted up one. Average: D+2.5 across eight polls ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/08/politics/cnn-polls-ohio-iowa-senate-governor-midterms), [co/efficient, partisan sponsor](https://battlegrounds.coefficient.org/oh)). Statehouse News Bureau reports the tight race is forcing a Republican resource surge ([SNB](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivAFBVV95cUxQSXRITnM0MUhLS3NGeXlyRENrX1NjTG5TTWV2UkFid1dUTjJqSHRGVVBWVmpPRndRc3ZTaWZRLWtYcjFaZ1Uyci05dnlETjBLNEFfb2hQSXV3UFdWbllndEROQ0NJTmhiYjFjYzBNSWQ1dTd3UDdHQ2JERXhuOWdTajd3b1RSZFY5NUNDenZPVVNTMkdiWW5UNFlnZUIwVWJJd3hmQ0xTS2x2ZXpNMjY0Z2JWaUZSYmNMcnlHRA?oc=5)).
- **Iowa Senate (Tossup).** Emerson has Ashley Hinson 46.6, Josh Turek 45.0 among likely voters through Oct. 6 (n=650); CNN/SSRS has Hinson up two. Average: D+0.5 across five polls ([Emerson](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1mKToIlrAwY0ehEA60PVFemP5WjwxsTxN/edit?rtpof=true&sd=true), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/08/politics/cnn-polls-ohio-iowa-senate-governor-midterms)).
- **Kansas Senate (Tossup).** Two public polls, Wedgewood Sept. 24 and Emerson Sept. 16, both show Adam Hamilton up two on Roger Marshall ([Emerson](https://emersoncollegepolling.com/kansas-2026/)). NYT calls it a surprisingly competitive race in a deep-red state ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/09/us/politics/kansas-senate-race-2026-marshall-hamilton.html)).
- **Michigan Senate (Lean D).** Polling averages D+3.9 over 11 polls; Mitchell Research has El-Sayed 46, Rogers 41 among likely voters, Oct. 1 (n=682) ([Mitchell](https://wwmt.com/news/michigan-politics/mitchell-poll-michigan-us-senate-election-abdul-el-sayed-mike-rogers-politics-government-vote-polls-state)). NBC News reports AIPAC's super PAC has resumed spending; the Detroit News reports the race is the most expensive in state history ([NBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxQcUdhUXdHb1RmOHJMUmFPWjhwN3U2OVN6bHdyYW8zdWRtVk5qVkN1Z0FqMDhIYVJFNnNaaDhfVm1TZ0FyVjlvYzNFSGFiQ3U3Mm9MelY0dERTSkp2Znl5RFVRQy1vanV5aW84SzZQTzl2TTlNLVAzdVFmRzNmMkRwRjFKaVBZU3FzdVVXRThJYkFydWFNNk14MFZ1ZjhzYVJUOGVyTmN6aEZDTHQ4ekQ4?oc=5), [Detroit News](https://news.google.?oc=5)).

## What the spectrum is saying

- **Center-left (NYT and NPR reporting):** some Republicans are rejecting Trump's move to import Russian diesel before the midterms ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/10/us/politics/republicans-midterms-trump-diesel-russia.html)). NPR reports from Ohio's 9th, where a DCCC internal shows Marcy Kaptur in a dead heat ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/10/nx-s1-5965798/on-the-ground-in-ohios-9th-district-the-battleground-shaping-next-months-midterms)).
- **Center-right (WSJ reporting):** a growing group of Republicans are warning, privately and publicly, that the party will perform poorly in November ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/trump-midterm-election-strategy-e4cfea75)).
- **Right (Ruthless, opinion):** the hosts argue El-Sayed's deleted posts and DSA ties are a hidden liability in Michigan, and that Tim Walz's fraud problem could cost Democrats a Minnesota seat ([feed](https://feeds.megaphone.fm/FOXM5875505224)).
- **Left (Pod Save America, opinion):** David Axelrod frames the Democrats' closing argument around affordability ([episode](https://audioboom.com/posts/8962811)).
- **Center (Silver Bulletin, opinion):** Nate Silver's FLIPR midterm forecast is live alongside his generic-ballot tracker ([forecast](https://www.natesilver.net/p/nate-silver-2026-midterm-election-polls-model)).

## Talking points

- The generic ballot averages D+7.2 across four polls, led by Pew at D+8 among registered voters (Oct. 4) and CBS/YouGov at D+9 among likely voters (Oct. 2); presidential approval averages 36.5 approve, 62.0 disapprove ([Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/with-americans-in-a-sour-mood-democratic-voters-are-more-engaged-in-midterms), [CBS](https://assets1.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/cms/prod_cms_alt/file/2026/10/04/0957ee32-a848-4872-b659-14303d3d3734/cbsnews_20261004_sun.pdf)).
- The Senate runs through six Republican-held consensus Tossups: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Texas, and the Ohio special. Democrats need a net gain of four ([Senate ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)).
- Data centers are arguably the top issue in Ohio and Michigan races, per WSJ, and Sherrod Brown has put them at the center of his populist pitch, per the Guardian ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/elections/will-voters-punish-politicians-for-data-centers-ask-ohio-and-michigan-1923848b), [Guardian](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifkFVX3lxTE1aRGswaVVSTjVWUFNzOGdYZnNmd3BfVkRFTjRhcWJaeF92dHBxLWp4THpoNUdCeUM2bUtIRjc0ZjhoRUFVelNhcmdWQUR2QTNoVXZDU2dDNk5wS3YxaDFsNV8yUlc5eDdLeU5DblBZLXVkQnJxV0hocnRlcHhpQQ?oc=5)).

## Coverage note

All 24 sources reported. Kalshi returned no priced markets (optional source). Four House races have polls whose candidate parties could not be resolved from today's headlines: FL-22, MT-01, SC-01, TX-35.
